<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914293_theRebbe_757" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914293_theRebbe_757__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section describes the daily divine service of a person, beginning with faith, progressing through contemplation, and culminating in self-nullification, which empowers one to transform the darkness of the material world into sweetness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And in a similar manner is the service of man each and every day,</t>
    <t s="2">“Man goes forth to his work and to his labor until the evening,”</t>
    <t s="3">that the service at the beginning of the day is in the aspect of faith,</t>
    <t s="4">“I gratefully thank You… great is Your faithfulness,”</t>
    <t s="5">and also at the beginning of prayer they say, “Give thanks to God,”</t>
    <t s="6">mere thanksgiving.</t>
    <t s="7">And afterwards is the service of contemplation and comprehension in Pesukei d’Zimra,</t>
    <t s="8">and particularly in the blessings of Shema and Shema.</t>
    <t s="9">And after this is the self-nullification of the Shemoneh Esrei,</t>
    <t s="10">which is utter self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="11">like the self-nullification of faith</t>
    <t s="12">(except that this faith is the faith that comes after comprehension).</t>
    <t s="13">And with the power of all this, “Man goes forth… to his labor until the evening,”</t>
    <t s="14">that he performs his service throughout the entire day until evening, according to the simple interpretation of “until the evening,”</t>
    <t s="15">and also the interpretation of “until the evening” from the term “evening” meaning sweetness and pleasantness,</t>
    <t s="16">for through engaging</t>
    <t s="17">(throughout the entire day)</t>
    <t s="18">in the matters of this physical world, than which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="19">which in themselves are in the aspect of evening and darkness,</t>
    <t s="20">and transforming them into holiness,</t>
    <t s="21">behold, through this is brought about true sweetness and pleasantness,</t>
    <t s="22">for when one transforms a bitter thing into something sweet, it is a greater sweetness than when it is sweet from its beginning.</t>
    <t s="23">And through this, “Man goes forth to his work and to his labor until the evening”</t>
    <t s="24">(also according to its simple meaning),</t>
    <t s="25">that his activity and service throughout the entire day until evening is in perfection,</t>
    <t s="26">for he has heavenly assistance,</t>
    <t s="27">and assistance in perfection,</t>
    <t s="28">in all the details of his service.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the concept of the Sukkah as a surrounding light (makif), which is drawn inward through the seven days of Sukkot, culminating in Shemini Atzeret with a higher encompassing light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is “In sukkot you shall dwell,”</t>
    <t s="2">that first there must be the matter of the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="3">the aspect of a surrounding light (makif).</t>
    <t s="4">And this very thing</t>
    <t s="5">(the making of the surrounding light of the sukkah),</t>
    <t s="6">even before the fulfillment of the commandment “In sukkot you shall dwell”</t>
    <t s="7">(and particularly before it is drawn into settlement),</t>
    <t s="8">is a matter of supreme loftiness</t>
    <t s="9">[as is also evident from what is said,</t>
    <t s="10">“The festival of sukkot you shall make for yourself,”</t>
    <t s="11">that there is a commandment also in the making of the sukkah].</t>
    <t s="12">And particularly according to what is explained in the discourses of the Baal HaHilula,</t>
    <t s="13">that the sechach (roof covering) of the sukkah</t>
    <t s="14">[which is the essence of the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="15">and the sukkah is named after the sechach]</t>
    <t s="16">is made from the cloud of the incense of Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="17">and it is known</t>
    <t s="18">also that sechach in gematria is one hundred, corresponding to the one hundred sounds of the shofar that it is the custom</t>
    <t s="19">of Israel</t>
    <t s="20">(for the custom of Israel is Torah)</t>
    <t s="21">to blow on Rosh Hashanah.</t>
    <t s="22">And also the details of the sounds are hinted at in the letters of sechach,</t>
    <t s="23">the letter samech (60) for the sounds of tekiah,</t>
    <t s="24">the letter chaf (20) for the sounds of shevarim and the letter chaf (20) for teruah.</t>
    <t s="25">And this means that the drawing down on Rosh Hashanah</t>
    <t s="26">(what is drawn down through the one hundred sounds)</t>
    <t s="27">is in a manner of “in the throne”</t>
    <t s="28">(in concealment),</t>
    <t s="29">and afterwards it comes to revelation</t>
    <t s="30">(for the day of our festival)</t>
    <t s="31">on the festival of Sukkot</t>
    <t s="32">in the sechach of the sukkah.</t>
    <t s="33">For all this is the advantage of the surrounding light of the sukkah as it is in itself.</t>
    <t s="34">And afterwards there must be “In sukkot you shall dwell,”</t>
    <t s="35">to draw down the surrounding light of the sukkah into settlement and inwardness,</t>
    <t s="36">and this drawing down must be for seven days, which include all the days of the encompassing,</t>
    <t s="37">and through this it is drawn afterwards on Shemini Atzeret</t>
    <t s="38">(that the surrounding light enters into inwardness and “atzaret” [gathers],</t>
    <t s="39">and is drawn down)</t>
    <t s="40">a higher surrounding light,</t>
    <t s="41">the aspect of the eighth day which guards the encompassing,</t>
    <t s="42">that nevertheless it is said,</t>
    <t s="43">“On the eighth day, an atzeret shall be for you,”</t>
    <t s="44">“They shall be yours alone, and no stranger with you.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the drawing down of the sukkah's surrounding light into inwardness is primarily accomplished through the Four Species, which symbolize unity and the aspect of Daat (knowledge).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is also the connection of taking the Four Species to the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="2">and as mentioned above, that the commandment of taking the Four Species in the sukkah is the optimal way to fulfill the commandment,</t>
    <t s="3">for the drawing down of the surrounding light of the sukkah into the aspect of inwardness and settlement is accomplished primarily through taking the Four Species.</t>
    <t s="4">And this will be understood based on what is explained in the Siddur</t>
    <t s="5">and in the discourses of the Baal HaHilula,</t>
    <t s="6">that these Four Species allude to the matter of unity.</t>
    <t s="7">For regarding the lulav it is written, “branches of date palms,”</t>
    <t s="8">and our sages, of blessed memory, expounded</t>
    <t s="9">that it must be “bound,”</t>
    <t s="10">that all the leaves</t>
    <t s="11">(even though in essence they are separate from each other)</t>
    <t s="12">must be attached and held together as if they are one,</t>
    <t s="13">and also each leaf is doubled from two,</t>
    <t s="14">meaning that the two leaves within it join and unite into one leaf.</t>
    <t s="15">And so it is with the hadassim, which are called “a branch of a leafy tree,”</t>
    <t s="16">specifically “leafy,”</t>
    <t s="17">three in one cluster.</t>
    <t s="18">And so it is with the willows of the brook, which grow in brotherhood.</t>
    <t s="19">And all the more so with the etrog, which remains on its tree from year to year,</t>
    <t s="20">that not only does it endure all the changes of the air of the four seasons of the year</t>
    <t s="21">(summer and winter, cold and heat),</t>
    <t s="22">but it also grows from all these four airs.</t>
    <t s="23">And furthermore, its growth to perfection</t>
    <t s="24">(of the etrog)</t>
    <t s="25">is over the course of three years,</t>
    <t s="26">meaning that the aforementioned matter</t>
    <t s="27">(that it endures all the changes of the airs and also grows from them)</t>
    <t s="28">is renewed in it three times,</t>
    <t s="29">for three times establishes a chazakah (presumption).</t>
    <t s="30">Based on this, it will be understood that the drawing down of the surrounding light</t>
    <t s="31">(of the sukkah)</t>
    <t s="32">into inwardness is accomplished primarily through taking the Four Species,</t>
    <t s="33">for the matter of unity in the Four Species indicates the aspect of Daat</t>
    <t s="34">(therefore, through them the aspect of Daat is drawn down,</t>
    <t s="35">as mentioned above from the writings of the AriZal).</t>
    <t s="36">And it is analogous to what is in man,</t>
    <t s="37">that one who has mature intellect (mochin d’gadlut) and broad knowledge (daat) can also endure opposites.</t>
    <t s="38">And particularly, the unity in the Four Species,</t>
    <t s="39">and especially in the etrog,</t>
    <t s="40">is not only that it endures opposites,</t>
    <t s="41">but that the opposites become one reality,</t>
    <t s="42">which indicates an abundance of Daat.</t>
    <t s="43">Therefore, the drawing down of the surrounding light of the sukkah into inwardness is accomplished primarily through taking the Four Species,</t>
    <t s="44">for Daat is a matter of inwardness,</t>
    <t s="45">as explained in the Tanya at the end and conclusion of chapter three</t>
    <t s="46">regarding the advantage of Daat over Chochmah and Binah, that Daat is a term of connection, etc.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
